claims.statement: Mystique achieves a success rate of 0.954 at function level and 0.924 at CVE level on the patch porting dataset.

claims.evidence_quote: Mystique markedly outperforms it in the Succ rate at CVE and function level by 0.539 (140%) and 0.404 (73.5%)

claims.statement: In cross-LLM porting, Mystique-StarCoder improves function-level Succ from 0.550 to 0.806 and CVE-level Succ from 0.385 to 0.710 over PPatHF-StarCoder.

claims.statement: In cross-project porting, Mystique achieves function-level Succ of 0.894 (L./O.) and 0.950 (O./L.), compared to PPatHF's 0.357 and 0.447.
Mystique successfully ported patches for 34 real-world vulnerable branches, with 29 successfully merged.

overall_conclusion: Mystique, an LLM-based patch porting approach with semantic/syntactic signature extraction and iterative checking-refining, achieves 0.954 function-level and 0.924 CVE-level success, outperforming TSBPORT by 13.2% and 12.3% respectively. It also demonstrates better generality across LLMs, projects, bugs, and Java, and successfully ports 34 real-world vulnerable branches.
comparable_notes: Fair comparison should use the same 694 CVE / 1,359 function patch porting dataset and the same fine-tuning split (pre/post CodeLlama release date). PPatHF was fine-tuned on a larger commit-history dataset (23,561 Linux + 7,913 other commits) rather than the same patch porting task. FixMorph was evaluated only on Linux subset due to compilation constraints. Metrics include Exact Match, Success (semantic equivalence), Failure rate, and Code BLEU; success is based on semantic equivalence to manually ported patches.
